title: Realtime is an enhancement that degrades to local-only; the websocket URL is derived from the GraphQL url
content:
## URL derivation

The websocket endpoint is derived from the client's `url`: `http` becomes `ws`, `https` becomes `wss`, and `/subscriptions` is appended. For a Switchboard on `http://localhost:4001/graphql` that is `ws://localhost:4001/graphql/subscriptions`. There is **one socket server for the whole Switchboard**, not one per subgraph. Override it with the `subscriptionsUrl` prop, or set `realtime={false}` where there is no websocket to talk to.

The first `subscribe` opens **one** websocket for all subscribers and subscribes to `documentChanges` with no `search` argument. The server sends every change the connection may read, and the client applies each subscriber's filter on the way out. Because the `DocumentCache` the provider builds subscribes in its constructor, the socket opens as soon as the provider mounts.

## Degradation, not dependency

Realtime is an enhancement, never a dependency. A socket that cannot be opened or is refused is **logged once and then ignored**, and the app keeps working on the changes it makes itself — every successful `create`, `execute` and `deleteDocument` emits a local change event, which is what makes the cache invalidate after a dispatch with no websocket involved.

The failed socket is **closed rather than kept**, so the next component to subscribe tries again. But — and this is the trap — **nothing subscribes on sign-in of its own accord**. An app on a Switchboard that refuses anonymous subscribers and that authenticates *after* mount will have had its one subscribe attempt refused, and will then sit with no realtime indefinitely. The fix is to **remount the provider** once the user is in.

## Socket auth

Auth on the socket reuses the same `tokenProvider`, sent as the **lowercase `authorization` connection param**, and re-resolved on every reconnect. A Switchboard with auth enabled refuses a connection that arrives without it, so an anonymous subscriber gets no realtime there.

One cosmetic consequence of the dual event sources: own writes are announced twice — once locally, once by the server push — so the cache refetches twice. Harmless.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/08-ReactorBrowserClient/02-ApiReference.md and 01-OverviewAndQuickstart.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
